replacements.old: Shape normalization is not a physical emission model. An X-ray prediction also requires the heavy-ion charge-state distribution, charge-exchange cross sections, neutral coma, and instrument response. The light curve was not used to calibrate the reconstructed wind. Correlation across a small number of frames does not establish predictive accuracy.
replacements.new: Emission-model limits. Converting proton flux to an X-ray count rate requires heavy-ion abundances and charge states, charge-exchange cross sections, the neutral coma and the detector response. The wind was reconstructed without fitting the eight X-ray rates. Their correlation with proton flux is a variability diagnostic with limited statistical power.

scienceReplacements.application: Apply exact string substitutions after any science/animation rebuild and before packaging or document hashing. scripts/apply_editorial_metadata.py applies them recursively without analysis reruns. The spacecraft replacement includes model / observation ratios, so remove the duplicate app callout sentence.

replacements.old: Claude only: transferred 12-member DA-design 16th–84th percentiles, not a calibrated confidence interval.
replacements.new: Claude: transferred 12-member assimilation-design 16th–84th percentiles. Probability coverage has not been calibrated.

replacements.old: Common copied preprint spacecraft data and common finite-hour masks, 19 Nov–5 Dec 2025. Argon and Claude assimilated these spacecraft; this is an in-sample calibration assessment. Codex calibration also used spacecraft information. These residuals do not establish independent forecast skill.
replacements.new: The models are compared with spacecraft measurements on the same finite hourly samples, 19 Nov–5 Dec 2025. Argon and Claude assimilated these spacecraft; Codex also used spacecraft data in calibration. These residuals therefore include calibration performance. Ratios give model / observation.

replacements.old: Claude’s independently computed coronal boundary compared pixelwise with remote-sensing-derived WSA maps. A model–model replication, not direct solar-wind observation. Argon and Codex adopt archived WSA maps, so no independent coronal-replication score is invented for them.
replacements.new: Claude’s independently computed PFSS/SCS/WSA boundary is compared pixel by pixel with archived WSA maps derived from remote sensing. This tests coronal-model agreement. Argon and Codex use the archived maps as input and have no separate coronal replication.

replacements.old: GONG photospheric magnetograms constrain PFSS/SCS topology; WSA converts open-field expansion and coronal-hole distance to an empirical speed map near 0.1 AU. This is a model input shared by the reconstruction families, not an in-situ measurement.
replacements.new: GONG photospheric magnetograms constrain PFSS/SCS topology. WSA converts open-field expansion and coronal-hole distance into an empirical speed map near 0.1 AU. All three reconstruction families use this modeled boundary input.

replacements.old: Standard gamma=2, t=0.1 setup. Claude retained a plot and error table, but no numeric 1D profile in its final workspace; its convergence is shown separately. Codex native CT kernel matches production, but this benchmark uses higher-order PPM/RK3 rather than production PLM/RK2. Brio–Wu admits nonunique compound-wave branches; no curve is called a unique exact solution.
replacements.new: Standard gamma=2, t=0.1 setup. Claude retained a plot and error table but no numerical 1D profile; its refinement errors are shown separately. Codex uses the production CT kernel with higher-order PPM/RK3 reconstruction and time integration; production uses PLM/RK2. Brio–Wu admits multiple compound-wave branches, so the plotted references are identified by method and resolution.

replacements.old: Self-reference resolutions and tests differ, so the error amplitudes are not a common leaderboard. Shocks reduce global order toward one. Codex historical GLM Brio–Wu errors are deliberately excluded from the final CT comparison.
replacements.new: The test definitions and self-reference resolutions differ between models. Compare refinement trends within each series. Shock discontinuities reduce global convergence order toward one. The Codex series includes only the selected CT formulation.

replacements.old: Analytic references use each benchmark’s archived boundary and pressure convention. The two benchmark setups differ. Codex’s final CT verification is its native flux/geometry audits plus selected numerical controls, not the superseded GLM Parker tests.
replacements.new: Each analytic reference uses its benchmark’s archived boundary and pressure convention. The two setups differ. Codex verifies its final CT implementation through separate flux/geometry audits and the recorded numerical controls below.

replacements.old: Different benchmarks, references, precisions, pressure conventions and aggregation rules are identified per panel. There is no defensible single numerical-quality rank.
replacements.new: Each panel identifies its benchmark, reference solution, precision, pressure convention and aggregation rule. These differences limit comparisons of error magnitude across models.

replacements.old: Native flux × true native-plane heliocentric radius² in AU²; a structure-contrast view, not an alternate absolute flux.
replacements.new: Native proton flux multiplied by the squared heliocentric radius in its source sampling surface, in AU². This compensates for radial geometric dilution to show stream structure.

replacements.old: Only the base 160-cell run has retained movie slices. The displayed comet comparison uses the fine 224-cell run. The CUDA producer samples a conical shell at the comet latitude −6.455°, not an equatorial plane; it cannot supply a true ecliptic-plane sample.
replacements.new: Retained movie slices are available for the 160-cell baseline run. The quantitative comet comparison uses the 224-cell fine run. The animation samples the solar-latitude cone at −6.455° and projects it onto the display axes; an ecliptic slice would require additional output.

replacements.old: The retained slices contain density and radial speed, not the full velocity vector. The native animation uses n_p v_r; it is an approximation to n_p |v| and remains labeled as such.
replacements.new: The retained density and radial-speed slices give radial proton flux n_p v_r. The full velocity vector required for n_p |v| was not retained.

replacements.old: All three reconstructions predict enhanced proton flux during at least part of the XMM visit, but they place the stream compression at different times.
replacements.new: The reconstructions differ in the timing and duration of the stream compression during the XMM observation.
replacements.reason: Remove an enhancement claim with no stated reference level.
Use the established distinction between geometric and photon-arrival epochs.
Use the same concrete terms as the provenance page.
Identify the tabulated bulk speed as heliocentric solar-wind speed, distinct from comet-relative incident speed.

replacements.old: Solar-wind charge exchange couples the neutral density nₙ to the ion density, relative speed, charge-state fraction f_q, cross section σ_CX, and photon yield Y_X. A proton-flux curve constrains one part of this expression.
replacements.new: Here nₙ is the neutral density, nₚ is the proton density, and f_q = n_q/nₚ is the emitting-ion abundance relative to protons, including elemental abundance and charge-state fraction. The emission also depends on relative speed, charge-exchange cross section σ_CX and photon yield Y_X.
replacements.reason: The displayed n_p f_q equation requires f_q to include emitting-element abundance, not only the fraction in a charge state.

replacements.old: Benchmark scope. Each pass applies to the specified pair of configurations. The models use different resolutions, precisions, closures and reference solutions, so their errors require separate interpretation. Claude’s retained Brio–Wu data contain an error table but no numerical profile. The Codex table includes failed controls.
replacements.new: Control criteria. PASS/FAIL flags apply to the listed configuration pairs and their recorded criteria. Failed Codex controls remain in the table. Each benchmark chart identifies its numerical method and reference solution.
replacements.reason: Shorten caveat duplicated in benchmark chart notes; retain the scope of pass/fail criteria.
